Reviewer Comment: The manuscript covers too many areas and the central scientific claims are not validated with sufficient rigor.
The NILM evaluation protocol and the meaning of cross-dataset generalization are unclear.
Evaluation on separately trained models across SustDataED2, REFIT, and UK-DALE is multi-dataset validation, not necessarily cross-dataset generalization.
The paper should add REFIT-to-UK-DALE, UK-DALE-to-REFIT, leave-one-house-out, unseen-house, zero-shot, and limited-adaptation evaluations.
The methodological novelty of EDTCN and the device-type-weighted focal loss is not isolated.
The mathematical formulation of the device-type-weighted focal loss is incomplete, including weight derivation, class weights, focusing parameter, normalization, and threshold selection.
It is unclear how focal loss, conventionally used for classification, is combined with appliance power regression.
A component-level statistical comparison is needed to demonstrate that EDTCN is more than a standard dilated TCN with empirical weighting.
The real-time execution claim is unclear because inference takes approximately 111 seconds.
A 21-minute context window processed in 111 seconds may still introduce substantial output delay.
CPU utilization approaches 100 percent, so concurrent metrology, FFT, display, tamper detection, communication, and storage must be evaluated.
The Discussion should be more argumentative and explain why the tested results were achieved.
The literature review should include recent work on intelligent energy management, optimization-assisted forecasting, nonlinear dynamics, hybrid deep learning, and AI-based estimation.
Active-power reduction is reported inconsistently as 71.59 percent and 92.6 percent.
Table 2 reports 695.68 mA at 5 V as 2.71 W, which is numerically inconsistent.
The abstract reports a 3���5 dollar cost while Table 2 reports a development-board price of approximately 16 do
A complete bill of materials should be provided for the deployable meter.
The paper should report total system power, including processor, STPM33, display, analog front end, storage, communication, and power-supply losses.
The manuscript should state whether the 0.513 W figure includes the TFT display and metrology components.
The phrase without FPU support should clarify whether software-emulated floating-point preprocessing occurs before INT8 inference.
The EDTCN architecture should be presented in a complete layer-by-layer table.
The receptive-field calculation resulting in 127 timesteps should be derived explicitly.
The mapping of 127 timesteps to 21 minutes depends on a 10-second sampling interval and must be stated clearly.
Dataset preprocessing needs details on missing values, resampling, normalization, synchronization, thresholds, activation filtering, periods, and voltage systems.
Evaluation should include normalized disaggregation error and signal aggregate error in addition to MAE and F1.
Results should be reported separately for each appliance rather than relying mainly on dataset-level averages.
The relatively low REFIT and UK-DALE F1 scores should be discussed critically.
The claim of near-perfect state detection should be removed unless it applies to all relevant appliances.
The 30.6 percent precision problem needs its exact experimental setting and appliance distribution explained.
The cloud LSTM forecasting module is weakly connected to the edge-NILM contribution.
A forecasting MAE of 12.70 W cannot be interpreted without scale, horizon, and baseline performance.
Cold-start adaptation and EWC are discussed, but the actual adaptation protocol is not fully described.
The dishwasher MAE reduction from over 100 W to approximately 1 W after adaptation is unusually large and requires validation against leakage or overfitting.
Hardware comparison should use equivalent workloads and identical peripherals.
Power measurement methodology should specify instrument, sampling interval, averaging period, uncertainty, voltage stability, and peripheral activity.
Thermal measurements should be included during sustained inference.
Long-duration stability should be evaluated for memory leakage, thermal throttling, filesystem reliability, and inference drift.
The custom PCB should be shown clearly and distinguished from the MangoPi development board.
Electrical safety, isolation distance, creepage, clearance, surge protection, and relevant smart-meter standards should be discussed before claiming industrial viability.
Client-side JWT routing alone does not prevent unauthorized backend access.
Stripe integration alone does not establish PCI-DSS compliance.
The paper should include failure-mode analysis for connectivity, reboot, model corruption, SPI failure, NAND corruption, power outage, and incorrect predictions.
Source code, trained models, firmware, quantization scripts, hardware files, and exact dataset splits should be available in a persistent repository.
Several figures contain text that is too small and should be redrawn with consistent notation.
The manuscript is excessively long and repetitive, especially in generic web-technology and smart-grid motivation sections.
Novelty against existing edge-based NILM systems is unclear and first claims should be supported by a concise technical comparison.
Performance improvements over Seq2Point, UNet-NILM, and BERT4NILM lack confidence intervals or significance testing.
Dataset splitting and cross-dataset evaluation need explicit description, including fine-tuning and dataset-specific optimization.
An ablation study is needed for dilated residual blocks, weighted focal loss, INT8 quantization, and compiler optimization.
MAE and F1 alone are insufficient; include precision, recall, SAE, and energy estimation accuracy with justification of metrics.
Privacy is discussed conceptually; residual risks and comparison with federated or encrypted approaches are not evaluated.
Scalability to thousands or millions of meters needs discussion of updates, maintenance, model synchronization, and reliability.
Harmonic measurements should be validated against a commercial or certified reference analyzer.
Inference latency must be aligned with the intended sampling interval and practical real-time operation.
The paper should discuss long-term robustness under changing household behavior and appliance inventories.
Computational complexity analysis is needed, including operations, memory footprint, parameters, and inference efficiency.
Implementation details needed for reproduction are missing, including seeds, software versions, repetitions, optimizer settings, schedules, and training hardware.
Cloud-assisted forecasting needs limitations analysis for connectivity loss, communication delay, and cloud interruption.
Hardware efficiency should use standardized metrics such as energy per inference and throughput per watt, not only power and cost.
The limitations and future-work section should cover three-phase systems, industrial environments, larger appliance sets, grid standards, cybersecurity, and long-term field validation.
